title: Unconventional Scaling of Electric Hall Effect in Magnetic Weyl Semimetals
authors: Chaoxi Cui, Yilin Han, Run-Wu Zhang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Yugui Yao
abstract: Electric Hall Effect (EHE), a unique phenomenon in two-dimensional (2D) magnetic systems, refers to the generation of Hall current by an out-of-plane electric field $\Ez$. Here, we demonstrate that for 2D magnetic Weyl semimetals that host doubly degenerate nodal points, the EHE features multiple unconventional scaling laws. At zero temperature, the EHE exhibits a topological $E_F^{-1}$ Fermi-energy scaling. Remarkably, the prefactor of the scaling is determined by the global topological charge of the point without any dependence on the local parameters of the system, leading to a universal and significant enhancement of Hall response in any species of Weyl points as the Fermi energy approaches the Weyl point. This significant response enables a weak electric field to be directly converted into a measurable Hall signal. Surprisingly, this enhanced Hall response is not diminished by temperature, but evolves into an unconventional logarithmically corrected scaling at finite temperature $σ_{xy}\propto\Ez\ln(1/|\Ez|)$ for weak $\Ez$, still yielding a divergent electric-field susceptibility. Thus, our work not only unveils intriguing scaling laws resulting from the interaction between magnetism and topology, but also suggests a novel scaling-enhanced and temperature-robust mechanism that may enable weak electric-field sensing through a practical and all-electric route.
summary: This work theoretically analyzes the Electric Hall Effect in magnetic Weyl Semimetals, revealing unique scaling behaviors dictated by topology. The key findings include universal $E_F^{-1}$ scaling at zero temperature and a logarithmically corrected scaling at finite temperatures. This suggests a robust, all-electric mechanism for sensing weak electric fields.
main_problem: The study investigates the unconventional scaling laws governing the Electric Hall Effect (EHE) in 2D magnetic Weyl Semimetals (WSMs). The goal is to understand how topology dictates this response, especially under weak electric fields.
main_result: The EHE exhibits universal scaling at zero temperature ($\chi_{xy} \propto E_F^{-1}$) and an unconventional logarithmically corrected scaling at finite temperature ($\sigma_{xy} \propto E_z \ln(1/|E_z|)$).
method: Theoretical derivation using the Kubo formula, Berry curvature calculations, and detailed scaling analysis involving momentum-to-parameter space mappings.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as 2D magnetic Weyl semimetals hosting doubly degenerate nodal points. The physics is captured by a two-band Hamiltonian subjected to an out-of-plane electric field ($E_z$) which acts as a mass term, inducing topological phase transitions.
key_observables: Electric Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$) and the intrinsic EHE coefficient ($\chi_{xy}$), both dependent on $E_F$ and $E_z$.
important_parameters: Fermi energy ($E_F$), out-of-plane electric field strength ($E_z$), and the global topological charge ($C$) of the Weyl points.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a two-band model approximation near the nodal points, and specific mathematical mappings between momentum space and parameter space are utilized for integration.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $E_z$-driven topological phase transition (gap closing) and compare numerical/analytical results showing the characteristic logarithmic scaling of $\sigma_{xy}(T)$ versus field strength.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the EHE coefficient ($\chi_{xy}$) at zero temperature using Berry curvature methods, then extends this analysis to finite temperatures by incorporating thermal effects into the conductivity calculation, revealing the unconventional scaling laws.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter topology, the concept of field-induced topological transitions and universal scaling laws are highly relevant in understanding quantum transport phenomena that can be modeled using effective Hamiltonians common in AMO physics (e.g., superconducting qubits or cavity QED systems exhibiting topological phases).
